briefdescription.para: getPassName - Return a nice clean name for a pass.

detaileddescription.para: This usually implemented in terms of the name that is registered by one of the Registration templates, but can be overloaded directly.

briefdescription.para: getPassID - Return the PassID number that corresponds to this pass.
doInitialization - Virtual method overridden by subclasses to do any necessary initialization before any pass is run.
doFinalization - Virtual method overriden by subclasses to do any necessary clean up after all passes have run.
print - Print out the internal state of the pass.

detaileddescription.para: This is called by Analyze to print out the contents of an analysis. Otherwise it is not necessary to implement this method. Beware that the module pointer MAY be null. This automatically forwards to a virtual function that does not provide the Module* in case the analysis doesn't need it it can just be ignored.

briefdescription.para: createPrinterPass - Get a Pass appropriate to print the IR this pass operates on (Module, Function or MachineFunction).
Each pass is responsible for assigning a pass manager to itself.

detaileddescription.para: PMS is the stack of available pass manager.

briefdescription.para: Check if available pass managers are suitable for this pass or not.
Return what kind of Pass Manager can manage this pass.
getAnalysisUsage - This function should be overriden by passes that need analysis information to do their job.

detaileddescription.para: If a pass specifies that it uses a particular analysis result to this function, it can then use the getAnalysis<AnalysisType>() function, below.

briefdescription.para: releaseMemory() - This member can be implemented by a pass if it wants to be able to release its memory when it is no longer needed.

detaileddescription.para: The default behavior of passes is to hold onto memory for the entire duration of their lifetime (which is the entire compile time). For pipelined passes, this is not a big deal because that memory gets recycled every time the pass is invoked on another program unit. For IP passes, it is more important to free memory when it is unused.
Optionally implement this function to release pass memory when it is no longer used.

briefdescription.para: getAdjustedAnalysisPointer - This method is used when a pass implements an analysis interface through multiple inheritance.

detaileddescription.para: If needed, it should override this to adjust the this pointer as needed for the specified pass info.

briefdescription.para: verifyAnalysis() - This member can be implemented by a analysis pass to check state of analysis information.
getAnalysisIfAvailable<AnalysisType>() - Subclasses use this function to get analysis information that might be around, for example to update it.

detaileddescription.para: This is different than getAnalysis in that it can fail (if the analysis results haven't been computed), so should only be used if you can handle the case when the analysis is not available. This method is often used by transformation APIs to update analysis results for a pass automatically as the transform is performed.

briefdescription.para: mustPreserveAnalysisID - This method serves the same function as getAnalysisIfAvailable, but works if you just have an AnalysisID.

detaileddescription.para: This obviously cannot give you a properly typed instance of the class if you don't have the class name available (use getAnalysisIfAvailable if you do), but it can tell you if you need to preserve the pass at least.

briefdescription.para: getAnalysis<AnalysisType>() - This function is used by subclasses to get to the analysis information that they claim to use by overriding the getAnalysisUsage function.
getAnalysis<AnalysisType>() - This function is used by subclasses to get to the analysis information that they claim to use by overriding the getAnalysisUsage function.

detaileddescription.para: If as part of the dependencies, an IR transformation is triggered (e.g. because the analysis requires BreakCriticalEdges), and Changed is non null, *Changed is updated.
Subclass this if you are an interprocedural optimization or you do not fit into any of the more constrained passes described below.
